response.query: Which multivariate joint-frequency selection algorithms (sparse multivariate spectral selection, group Lasso on cross-spectra, frequency-domain CCA) balance detection power and computational cost for high-dimensional features?
response.answer: Sparse multivariate spectral selection, group Lasso on cross-spectra, and frequency-domain CCA effectively balance detection power and computational cost for high-dimensional features. These methods are designed to handle large datasets efficiently while maintaining strong predictive performance.

results.content: While data of this nature have been available in large repositories such as the UK Biobank, large-scale genome-wide screens in a time-to-event setting have been extremely challenging due to various computational and statistical challenges.We applied our method, snpnet-Cox, that has proven to be an effective method for simultaneous variable selection and estimation in high-dimensional settings, to examine the genetic contributions to cardiometabolic disease progression, measured by time from disease diagnosis to time of complication/comorbidity diagnosed or procedure in the UK Biobank. MOTIVATION: The prediction performance of Cox proportional hazard model suffers when there are only few uncensored events in the training data.RESULTS: We propose a Sparse-Group regularized Cox regression method to improve the prediction performance of large-scale and high-dimensional survival data with few observed events.
